That is a single first-party Intel number against Arrow's existing unpacker. The benchmark is public in Arrow, but there is no CPU SKU, compiler or flags and no table, so C.

corrections.workload: Parquet dictionary-index decoding (BM_DictDecodingInt64_literals in parquet-encoding-benchmark) using bit-unpack with Ice Lake server (ICX) AVX-512 subsets (AVX512IFMA, AVX512VBMI, AVX512VNNI, AVX512VBMI2). A review comment notes that unpack32_avx512_icx() does not support num_bits > 16.
corrections.caveats: PR 14674 (ARROW-18362, by zhoudan-intel with Intel co-authors) was closed unmerged by amol- on 2023-03-30 for inactivity. The code (about 1,145 lines of AVX-512 intrinsics headers) lives only in the PR diff, not in the library, and pitrou was 'quite lukewarm' about maintaining it. There is a single headline number with no table, CPU SKU or compiler flags. The issue it relates to (14672) gives no numbers. The incumbent is Arrow's own unpacker, not varint, Simple8b or FastPFor. The record id is the whole apache/arrow repo, so this entry describes an unmerged patch rather than Arrow itself.

notes: The 55% claim matches the PR text, so C stands. tier_reason: The README says that, compared with bshuf_trans_bit_elem/bshuf_untrans_bit_elem from the classic implementation, 'this code yields a typical speedup between 1.3x and 10x'. The benchmark code is public (tests/bitshuffle_benchmark.cc, Google Benchmark against the classic kiyo-masui functions, built via BUILD.bazel), but no results table, CPU model, compiler or flags are given, so it is first-party with partial methodology: C.

corrections.caveats: The README gives a single range (1.3x to 10x) with no per-CPU table, no compiler flags and no CPU model. The benchmark harness does exist: tests/bitshuffle_benchmark.cc runs bitshuf_encode_block/bitshuf_decode_block against the classic bshuf_trans_bit_elem/bshuf_untrans_bit_elem for element sizes 1-18 and 63-66 and block sizes from 256 B to 256 MB, plus a memcpy reference. It uses SSE2/AVX2/AVX-512 with runtime dispatch that needs GNU IFUNC, and it is little-endian only. The library is adjacent to rather than inside integer bit-packing (bit transposition of typed arrays used as a compression pre-filter), so the category fit may be wrong. The baseline is another bitshuffle implementation, not varint, Simple8b or FastPFor. The license is dual Apache-2.0 OR MIT (LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT both present).

notes: The claim matches the README. The record wrongly said there was no benchmark code: it is tests/bitshuffle_benchmark.cc. The license files are LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT, which is why a plain LICENSE path returned 404. Last commit is 2024-01-22 (stale), 5 commits, and the repo is neither archived nor a fork.
